title: Milestones ahead
description: If you add your child's birth month to his profile, the app lets you know about a month before each important stage: starting school, the age of discernment, starting to teach prayer, first fasting, preparing for puberty, turning ten, the first phone and the identity question. Without it, you will find the stage guides in your library by your child's age group. Each stage comes with a short notification, a mini-guide of cards and links to what suits it in the app.

alert_policy.text: At most one notification per child per month; if two stages coincide, the more important one goes first and the other waits. Without a date of birth no notification is sent, and the cards appear in your library according to the child's age group.

evidence.text_ar: يا غلام سم الله وكل بيمينك وكل مما يليك
evidence.context: The Prophet ﷺ said this to Umar ibn Abi Salamah, a young boy, at a meal.
evidence.meaning: Young boy, say Bismillah (in the name of Allah), eat with your right hand, and eat from what is in front of you.

evidence.context: Narrated by Malik ibn al-Huwayrith; the Prophet ﷺ said it to a group of young men who stayed with him to learn.
evidence.meaning: Pray as you have seen me praying.

evidence.text_ar: إن الله رفيق يحب الرفق في الأمر كله
evidence.meaning: Allah is Gentle and loves gentleness in all matters.

evidence.text_ar: من نسي صلاة فليصل إذا ذكرها لا كفارة لها إلا ذلك
evidence.meaning: Whoever forgets a prayer, let him pray it when he remembers it; there is no expiation for it other than that.

evidence.text_ar: فكنا نصومه بعد ونصوّم صبياننا ونجعل لهم اللعبة من العهن فإذا بكى أحدهم على الطعام أعطيناه ذاك حتى يكون عند الإفطار
evidence.context: Al-Rubayyi' bint Mu'awwidh describing the fast of the day of Ashura in the Prophet's time.
evidence.meaning: We used to fast it afterwards and have our young children fast; we would make them toys of wool, and when one of them cried for food, we gave him that (toy) until it was time to break the fast.

evidence.text_ar: إن الله لا يستحيي من الحق فهل على المرأة من غسل إذا احتلمت
evidence.context: Umm Sulaym said this when asking the Prophet ﷺ; narrated by Umm Salamah.
evidence.meaning: Allah is not shy of the truth: is a woman required to take a ritual bath (ghusl) if she has a wet dream?

evidence.text_ar: كلكم راع وكلكم مسئول عن رعيته
evidence.meaning: Each of you is a shepherd, and each of you is responsible for his flock.

evidence.text_ar: خدمت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عشر سنين فما قال لي أف ولا لم صنعت ولا ألا صنعت
evidence.context: Anas ibn Malik describing his years of serving the Prophet ﷺ, which began when he was a boy.
evidence.meaning: I served the Prophet ﷺ for ten years, and he never once said to me 'uff' (a word of annoyance), nor 'why did you do that?', nor 'why didn't you do that?'

milestones.title: Starting school

alert.title: When school is near
alert.body: In many countries school starts at about six. A short guide to preparing your child for it calmly.

cards.title: Two to four weeks before
cards.body: Talk about school positively and concretely: what he will do there and who he will meet. Visit the building if you can, and read a story about a first school day together. Never use school as a threat, like 'you'll see what the teacher does to you'.

cards.title: Sleep and routine
cards.body: Move bedtime and wake-up time earlier gradually, about a quarter of an hour every few days, so that the first week isn't exhausting: a school-age child needs roughly 9 to 12 hours of sleep.

cards.title: The goodbye
cards.body: A short, warm, confident goodbye with a clear sign of your return: 'I'll come for you after the last lesson.' Don't slip away without saying goodbye, and don't go back in if he cries: some crying in the first days is normal and usually fades.

cards.title: After school
cards.body: Give him ten minutes of your full attention, ask specific questions like 'Who did you sit next to?' instead of 'How was school?', and let him rest and play before homework.

red_flags: Refusing school every morning for more than three to four weeks, or intense fear that does not ease.
Repeated stomach aches or headaches on school days only.
A clear step backwards that lasts weeks, such as wetting the bed again, or signs that he is being hurt or bullied → talk to the teacher and to the paediatrician or school counsellor.

alert.title: Approaching the age of discernment
alert.body: Your child now understands reasons and tells right from wrong better. Four steps to make the most of this stage.

cards.title: What changes?
cards.body: Around six or seven most children begin to understand right and wrong and the reasons behind rules, so explain the 'why' briefly instead of only giving orders. The exact definition and rulings of tamyeez belong to the scholars; what is here is upbringing.

cards.title: Asking permission and privacy
cards.body: Teach him to knock and ask permission before entering a room, especially at times when people rest; the verse shown here, from Surat an-Nur, concerns this manner. Read the story 'Aisha and the Adab of Isti'dhan' with him.

cards.title: Body safety
cards.body: Teach him the correct names of body parts, and that what underwear covers is private: no one may touch it or ask to see it, except someone helping him wash when needed, or a doctor with you present, and that there are no secrets from his parents, or whoever cares for him, about touch. Say it calmly, the way you teach road safety. And if he touches his body in front of others, remind him calmly that this is private, without scolding.

cards.title: Small responsibilities, manners taught gently
cards.body: A daily household job of his own, keeping promises, and correcting manners with short, kind words in the moment, as in the attached hadith, where a young boy was taught table manners in three short phrases.

alert.title: Turning seven next month
alert.body: At seven, teaching prayer begins, as in Prophetic guidance, and the Prayer Journey is ready for you: 12 weeks of small steps.

cards.title: Why seven?
cards.body: Well-known Prophetic guidance commands teaching children the prayer at seven and firmness about it at ten. Its wording mentions striking, which scholars restricted to what is neither harmful nor humiliating; this program does not use it, and relies on example, gradualness and gentleness. The guidance's source is in the linked knowledge unit, because this program only displays hadith from the two Sahihs. Before puberty, prayer is training, and the child is not blamed for it.

cards.title: The Prayer Journey
cards.body: Twelve weeks in six small stages: praying beside you, wudu, the words and movements of prayer, the prayer times, all five prayers, then 'praying on my own'. You assign, he records it in child mode, you confirm in the evening, and his coins turn into a real reward you promise him, while you tie prayer to the love of Allah, not to the reward alone.

cards.title: Be what he sees
cards.body: Children learn the prayer by watching, as in the attached hadith about it, so let him see you pray calmly and on time, and pray beside him.

cards.title: Gentleness first
cards.body: No shouting, no shaming, no comparison. Correct one thing at a time, in private, and if he misses a prayer, he prays it when he remembers it, with no lecture and no blame. Among the attached hadiths are one about gentleness in every matter and one about a forgotten prayer.

milestones.title: First fasting attempts

alert.title: Ramadan is a month away
alert.body: If your child will try fasting this year, here is how to start gently and safely. A child who has reached puberty must fast.

cards.title: Training, not obligation
cards.body: Fasting becomes obligatory at puberty; before that it is training. The attached hadith is the source for getting young children used to fasting and distracting them with play when they are hungry; it describes the fast of Ashura. We take the distraction and the encouragement from it, and a tired child breaks the fast at once.

cards.title: Start small
cards.body: Begin with a few hours after suhoor or an early breakfast, then until midday, and only increase after two or three comfortable days. For ages 7–9 a full day is not the goal; ages 10–12 may reach full days gradually, on rest days and no more than two a week. A child who has reached puberty, by menstruation or a wet dream, must fast as an obligation whatever their age, so the training cap does not apply. The fasting ladder in the Ramadan program sets the steps for each age.

cards.title: Suhoor, iftar and sleep
cards.body: Water little and often through the evening, a slow suhoor such as bread, oats, eggs, yoghurt or pitted, chopped dates instead of sweets, an iftar that starts with water, and an early bedtime: a tired child finds fasting hard.

cards.title: When to stop at once
cards.body: Dizziness, a severe headache, vomiting, unusual sleepiness, very little or very dark urine, or him saying, before puberty, that he can't go on: he breaks the fast with water and a date or some juice, and you praise his effort. Fainting, confusion or a seizure means emergency services at once, and nothing by mouth until he is fully alert.

cards.title: The doctor before fasting
cards.body: See a doctor before any fasting if the child has diabetes, kidney or heart disease or epilepsy, takes a regular medicine, is very underweight or has recently been ill. And keep an eye on older children: dieting to lose weight can hide behind fasting.

red_flags: Fainting, confusion or a seizure → emergency services at once; nothing by mouth until he is fully alert.
A chronic illness or a regular medicine → ask the doctor before any attempt.
Severe restriction of food, skipping iftar or preoccupation with weight, especially in older children → talk to a doctor.

milestones.title: Preparing for puberty: girls

alert.title: A calm talk before puberty
alert.body: Your daughter is nearing the age when puberty can begin. Talking before the first signs makes it a calm, safe stage for her.

cards.title: Talk before the signs
cards.body: The first signs of puberty usually appear between eight and thirteen, according to the American Academy of Pediatrics. Talk early, calmly and privately. Usually the mother or a trusted woman in the family leads the talk; if neither is available, the father can start it himself, calmly and respectfully. The message: your body is healthy and growing as Allah created it.

cards.title: What happens, and in what order?
cards.body: It usually starts with a small bump under the nipple, sometimes on one side before the other, then body hair (which sometimes comes first), a growth spurt, more sweating and skin changes. The first period usually comes about two to two and a half years after breast development begins.

cards.title: Getting ready for the first period
cards.body: A small bag with sanitary pads and spare underwear for school, showing her how to use and dispose of a pad, keeping a note of the dates, and knowing she can come to you at any hour without embarrassment.

cards.title: The religious side, gently
cards.body: With puberty she becomes responsible herself for prayer and fasting, and she learns the rulings of purity from a trustworthy female teacher or female scholar, or from a reliable source that scholars point you to. Modesty is good, as in one of the two attached hadiths, but it does not stop us from asking: in the other, Umm Sulaym asked the Prophet ﷺ about such matters directly.

cards.title: Feelings and respect
cards.body: Mood swings and sensitivity about her body are normal. No comments about her weight or shape from anyone in the family, respect her privacy in her room and in the bathroom, and be patient.

red_flags: Any sign of puberty before age eight → paediatrician: early puberty needs assessment.
No breast development by thirteen, or no period by fifteen or three years after breast development began → doctor.
Heavy bleeding that soaks a pad every one to two hours, bleeding that lasts more than seven days, or pain that stops her daily life → doctor.
Fainting or severe dizziness with the bleeding → emergency care immediately.

milestones.title: Preparing for puberty: boys

alert.title: A calm talk before puberty
alert.body: Your son is nearing the age when puberty can begin. A calm talk before the changes keeps him from learning about them from friends or the internet.

cards.title: Talk before the changes
cards.body: In boys, puberty usually begins between nine and fourteen, according to the American Academy of Pediatrics. Usually the father or a trusted man in the family leads the talk; if neither is available, the mother can start it herself, privately and calmly. If he doesn't hear it from you, he will hear it from friends or the internet.

cards.title: What happens?
cards.body: The testicles grow first, which parents usually don't notice, then hair appears in the pubic area and the armpits, a growth spurt comes, the voice cracks and then deepens, sweating increases and spots appear on the face. Slight swelling under one or both nipples is common in boys and usually goes away by itself within two years; if not, see a doctor.

cards.title: Wet dreams (ihtilam)
cards.body: Tell him before it happens that a release of fluid during sleep is a natural sign of growing up, not a sin and not an illness, and that it is a sign of puberty, from which he becomes responsible himself for prayer and fasting. The rules of purity and ghusl that follow, he should learn from a trustworthy teacher or scholar. Asking about such things is part of religion, as in Umm Sulaym's question in the attached hadith.

cards.title: Daily care and privacy
cards.body: A daily shower, deodorant, clean clothes, his own private space if possible, respect for his privacy in shared rooms, and knocking before entering, plus a calm talk about images and content online before he comes across them.

cards.title: Feelings and respect
cards.body: Mood swings, wanting more independence and caring about friends' opinions are normal. Modesty is a trait the attached hadith ties to faith, so teach it with respect, and never mock his changing voice or his body.

red_flags: Signs of puberty before nine, or none by fourteen → paediatrician.
Sudden pain or swelling in a testicle → emergency care immediately: it can be a twisted testicle.
Breast swelling that is large or lasts more than two years, or growth in height that stops → doctor.

alert.title: Turning ten next month
alert.body: A new stage: firmness with gentleness about prayer, more trust and more privacy. A short guide.

cards.title: Firmness with gentleness
cards.body: At ten, the well-known Prophetic guidance calls for firmness about prayer. Its wording mentions striking, which scholars restricted to what is neither harmful nor humiliating; this program does not use it. Its way of being firm is a steady routine, calm daily follow-up, conversation about meaning and your own example, with no shouting or shaming. Among the attached hadiths: gentleness in every matter, and Anas, who never heard a word of annoyance from the Prophet ﷺ in the ten years he served him.

cards.title: Prayer becomes his own
cards.body: If he has finished the Prayer Journey, he moves on to 'My prayer, my responsibility': he keeps track of his own prayer and you hold a short weekly check-in. If he hasn't started it yet, start now from the stage that suits him.

cards.title: Privacy at home
cards.body: His own bed, and his own room or private corner where possible, with knocking before entering, by parents too. Start the puberty conversations now; the puberty guide is in your library now.

cards.title: More trust, more responsibility
cards.body: Pocket money he manages himself, a household responsibility of his own, and a voice in family decisions. Each of us is a shepherd, as in one of the attached hadiths, so let him practise caring for what is his: his things, his time, and a younger sibling if there is one.

alert.title: Before the first phone
alert.body: Around eleven, many children ask for their first phone. Before you say yes or no: a four-step plan.

cards.title: Does he need it now?
cards.body: Many families hold off on a smartphone until there is a real need, such as a distant school or travel; 'all my friends have one' is not a need. A basic phone for calls, or a smartwatch that can only call the parents, is a reasonable first step. If your child already uses a tablet or a shared device, start these steps now.

cards.title: A written agreement first
cards.body: Write a short family agreement together, where every rule for him has a matching rule for you: no devices at the table for any of us, and all devices sleep outside the bedrooms.

cards.title: The internet licence
cards.body: Let him practise the 'internet licence' scenarios in the app, like a stranger asking for a photo or offering a gift, before he has his own device. The safe answer always includes telling a parent.

cards.title: Settings and the golden rule
cards.body: Parental controls and app approval at the start, no phone in the bedroom at night, and the most important rule of all: 'Tell me anything that bothers you, and I will listen without shouting or taking the phone away at once.'

milestones.title: The identity question

alert.title: Turning thirteen next month
alert.body: The question 'who am I?' begins now, and you are still the closest answer. A short guide to this stage.

cards.title: Who am I?
cards.body: Trying out new opinions, styles and friends is a normal part of building an identity, not a rejection of your values, and online worlds are part of that experiment too. Stay close and curious rather than alarmed.

cards.title: From control to supervision
cards.body: Rules agreed together, reasons explained, and freedom that grows with trust. You are still shepherds responsible for your flock, as in the attached hadith, but now the teenager walks beside you rather than behind you.

cards.title: Questions of faith are welcome
cards.body: A question or a doubt is a chance for conversation, not a disaster. Listen until he has finished, answer what you know, and look for answers together with scholars and in the app's paths on certainty.

cards.title: Belonging
cards.body: Give him a real role at home and in the community: at the mosque, in volunteering or in a skill he masters. Get to know his friends and their families: belonging protects more than surveillance does.

red_flags: Persistent sadness, withdrawing from family and friends, or a sharp drop in schoolwork for more than two weeks → talk to a doctor or a counsellor.
Any talk of self-harm or of not wanting to live → get professional help the same day.
If he has a plan or a means, or is in danger right now → emergency services at once; don't leave him alone, and remove medicines and dangerous tools.
Signs of substance use, or contact with a stranger who asks for secrecy → act at once, and calmly.
